title: Sell Mineral Rights in Kirby, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Kirby, WY | Hamilton Dome
metaDescription: Kirby, WY mineral owner near the Hamilton Dome field in Hot Springs County? Get a fair cash offer for your Bighorn Basin mineral interest.
heroLead: Kirby sits near Hamilton Dome, one of the Bighorn Basin's long-producing fields, in a stretch of Hot Springs County that's been quietly paying royalties for the better part of a century.
intro: Hamilton Dome was discovered in the 1920s and has been re-worked and re-drilled through multiple operator changes since. If your family's mineral interest sits in this area, it's likely been producing, at some level, longer than anyone currently living can remember firsthand.

sections.heading: Hamilton Dome's long, steady decline
paragraphs: Like most legacy Bighorn Basin fields, Hamilton Dome has settled into stripper-level production, small volumes from wells that keep going despite their age. Secondary recovery efforts over the decades have extended the field's life well beyond what the original discovery wells would have managed alone.

sections.heading: Ownership through a century of transfers
paragraphs: Interests here have typically passed through several generations of the same family, sometimes split among numerous heirs as estates settled over the decades. Small fractional interests are common, and untangling exactly what percentage you own is often the first real task before selling.

sections.heading: What determines your Kirby-area offer
paragraphs: Current production volume, decline trend, and whether your specific tract has seen recent workover activity. Bring your division order and recent check stubs; Hot Springs County Clerk records in Thermopolis can fill in any gaps in your paperwork.

sections.heading: What a division order tells you that a deed doesn't
paragraphs: Your original mineral deed shows what your family started with, but your division order shows what you're actually being paid on today, after any unitization, pooling, or ownership adjustments over the years. Both documents matter, and buyers want to see both if you have them.

faqs.question: Is Hamilton Dome field still producing?
faqs.answer: Yes, at stripper levels after nearly a century of production, with periodic secondary recovery work extending well life.

faqs.question: How many heirs typically split a Kirby-area interest?
faqs.answer: It varies, but multi-generational splits among several heirs are common on legacy Bighorn Basin tracts. A title check confirms your exact percentage.

faqs.question: What if my check amount has been shrinking?
faqs.answer: Natural decline is normal on a field this old. It's factored into any offer, not a sign of a problem with your interest.

faqs.question: What if my division order percentage doesn't match my deed?
faqs.answer: That's common after decades of unitization and pooling adjustments. The division order reflects your current payable interest and generally takes precedence for valuation purposes.
